about: Fixtures of known answer for the near-copy rule (exam_nocopy_v1_0_0.py, exam_nocopy_shapes_v1_0_0.ttl). All records are synthetic or taken verbatim from the course question bank; no student data. Each case gives the number of shared 4-word sequences, the number of 4-word sequences of the new item (C = shared / total), whether the correct answers are equal as normalised text, the listing relation, and whether the item is a near copy. The five variants carry design_c, the value printed in section 2.1 of exam_design_v1_0_0.md. S_values is item 0 of 08-tooling/ch01-page/question_bank_v1_1_1.json (the check compares it with the bank).

seeds.stem: Which statement about values in Python is correct?
options: Every expression reduces to a value, and its data type decides what can be done with it
Only numbers count as values, while text is handled by a separate mechanism in the language
The operator alone decides what type a value has, whatever the value is at that point
Data types matter only when a value is printed, and never when values are combined

seeds.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 5):
    total = total + n
print(total)

item.stem: Why can a value of any type be printed but not always added to a number?
options: Printing needs only text of the value, while adding needs the type to define the operator
Printing converts every value to a number first, which makes adding always possible
Adding is done by print, which has no rule about the types of the values it gets
Types are checked only when a program is saved, so a mismatch is found before the run
